findings.title: The populated work pack is populated in a shape the app's own hydrator throws away
findings.evidence: Ticket: 'One new dedicated fixture client id gets a distinct, populated pack' and AC1 'A cell proves two client ids' get_client_work_pack responses differ (one populated, one empty)'. apps/web/e2e/home-board-mock.mjs:99-124 gives each facet rows of {id, label, state, updated_at}. The door's wire contract (packages/db/migrations/0214_client_work_pack.sql:324-337 active arm, :365-390 recent_success arm) projects work_id, purpose, status, memo, attempts, current_run_status, retrying, created_at and (recent_success) committed_at, receipt_id, entry_id - and apps/web/lib/work/client-work-pack.ts:158-174 hydrateRow returns null for any row without work_id ('a row with no Work id cannot be linked to, so it is not a row'). Re-run here: hydrateClientWorkPack(POPULATED_WORK_PACK) -> {activeCount:1, activeRows:0, recentCount:1, recentRows:0}, i.e. a count of 1 with an EMPTY preview under preview_limit 5, a shape the real door cannot produce. The row 'state' values are wrong too: in_progress is not in accounting_work's status roster (packages/db/migrations/0178_accounting_work_journal_successor.sql:306-307: queued, running, awaiting_input, stopping, completed, refused, failed, cancelled, expired). The new cell cannot catch this because it asserts deepEqual against the very constant the mock returns (apps/web/e2e/e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts, '#902 - the dedicated fixture client reads the POPULATED pack'), so it proves scoping but nothing about contract fidelity.
findings.required_fix: Re-shape POPULATED_WORK_PACK's rows onto 0214's field names (work_id/purpose/status/memo/attempts/current_run_status/retrying/created_at, plus committed_at/receipt_id/entry_id for recent_success) with statuses from 0178's roster (e.g. running / completed), and assert on the HYDRATED pack (hydrateClientWorkPack) as well as the raw constant so the fixture cannot drift from the door again.

findings.title: The opener was widened only across === / !== spellings; a measured in-tree dispatch spelling claiming six verbs is still invisible
findings.evidence: Ticket: 'The opener pattern recognises every dispatch spelling measured across the current lane mocks plus the historical rpc === spelling', and the current-behaviour line 'A lane mock whose dispatch variable is spelled any way other than the three recognised shapes is invisible to the census; an undeclared shared verb in such a file passes silently.' The lane's measurement (final report, #863 row) was grep -noE '\b[a-zA-Z_]+ === "[a-z0-9_]+"', which by construction can only find === spellings. apps/web/e2e/home-board-mock.mjs:185-192 declares EMPTY_RPCS and :331 dispatches `if (request.method === "POST" && EMPTY_RPCS.includes(path))` - six RPC verbs claimed by a spelling RPC_VERB_OPENER still cannot see (verified by re-running the widened regex over that file: none of list_agent_act_receipts, list_bank_account_proposals, list_bank_accounts, list_bank_statements, list_fiscal_years, list_uncoded_filings is in its match set). FIVE of those six have a second claimant in another lane mock, each using a spelling the census DOES see: bank-close-registers-mock.mjs:225 (list_fiscal_years), :243 (list_agent_act_receipts); bank-match-mock.mjs:306 (list_bank_accounts), :312 (list_bank_statements); documents-viewer-mock.mjs:582 (list_uncoded_filings). So real multi-claimant verbs exist today that the widened census still reports as single-owner - the exact failure mode the ticket names. (The array-membership limit is acknowledged in prose in the home-board declaration comment, but that predates #863 and is not a gate.) The report's claim that the measurement 'found exactly one MORE real spelling in use' is therefore not supported.
findings.required_fix: Either widen the census to the array-membership spelling (an array literal of /rest/v1/rpc/<verb> strings consumed by .includes(path)), or add a cell that names those six verbs as a declared, reasoned exception so the claim is a gate rather than a comment. And state the measurement method honestly: a grep for '=== "' cannot find non-=== dispatch.

findings.title: The body-reader census matches two literal names plus request.on, so the drain shape every real violator used evades it under any other name
findings.evidence: Ticket: 'A census cell ... scans every *-mock.mjs source and fails if any defines its own request-body-reading function (a local request.on("data")/"end" pair, or a local readJson/readBody not imported from the shared module).' In apps/web/e2e/e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts, PRIVATE_BODY_READER_FUNCTION only matches `function readJson(` / `function readBody(`, and PRIVATE_BODY_READER_STREAM only matches request.on("data"|"end"). All seven real violators drained with `for await (const chunk of request)` - a shape the census never tests for, so a rename to drainBody would have passed. A live instance already sits inside LANE_MOCKS and passes the new census: apps/web/e2e/documents-intake-mock.mjs:172-174 `async function drain(request) { for await (const chunk of request) void chunk; }`, used at :478 for /rest/v1/rpc/list_unassigned_documents (answered unconditionally) and at :646 - an UNCACHED consumption of the very stream readCachedJson caches. The arrow form (`const readJson = async (request) => ...`) is also uncovered.
findings.required_fix: Add `for await (... of request)` and the arrow-assigned readJson/readBody form to the census's violation shapes, then decide documents-intake-mock.mjs's drain: repoint it onto readCachedJson, or declare it with a stated reason the way the file's sibling declarations do.

findings.title: AC1's GREEN-after-correction half is not built
findings.evidence: Ticket AC1: 'A cell feeds the census a synthetic mock source ... that uses a non-standard dispatch spelling and an undeclared shared verb; the census is RED before the widening and GREEN after the synthetic source is corrected.' The fix round's cell ('RPC-opener census - a synthetic rpc === claimant and a synthetic path !== claimant of the SAME undeclared verb are BOTH extracted AND flagged as a collision') carries the RED half all the way to verbCollisions, but no cell shows the same synthetic pair going GREEN once corrected (one claimant, or the pair added to a declared share). Without that half, a verbCollisions that flagged everything would still pass this cell.
findings.required_fix: Add the counter-half: the same two synthetic sources with the collision removed (single claimant, or both names on a declared share) must produce zero problems.

findings.title: AC3 is met by arming the refusal, not by owner-only dispatch or a forced lower rank
findings.evidence: Ticket AC3: 'The mock enforces owner-only dispatch, or the door refusal renders when a lower rank is forced.' apps/web/e2e/journal-work-mock.mjs:977-981 adds control op egress_reactivate_answer, and the handler answers CLR04 'insufficient role' purely because state was armed (:1487-1490) - it never inspects the caller, and every cell in journal-work-walk.spec.ts signs in as the same owner persona. The walk cell (apps/web/e2e/journal-work-walk.spec.ts:914) records this openly as a RECORDED SUBSTITUTION, so the report is honest, but the cell proves the rendering path, not the floor: it would stay green if the door's owner floor disappeared. Branch (a) is reachable in principle - serve-built.mjs:579-593 already derives rank from the sign-in email prefix (owner@/bookkeeper@/viewer@) - but only through serve-built.mjs, a shared file the work order's rule 7 tells lanes to keep minimal.
findings.required_fix: Either accept the substitution explicitly at integration (record it on the ticket rather than only in a code comment), or expose the signed-in persona's rank to lane mocks once in serve-built.mjs and let the mock DERIVE the CLR04 answer instead of being told it.

findings.title: The p_work filter is applied AFTER the page is assembled and silently disables pagination - the one shape 0202 says it avoids
findings.evidence: Ticket: 'When p_work is present, the mock returns only rows whose work_id matches it, mirroring migration 0202's server-side predicate (p_work is null or work_id = p_work).' apps/web/e2e/activity-mock.mjs:318-328 filters the already-assembled PAGE_1 and then forces next_cursor: null, truncated: false whenever p_work is present. 0202 applies the predicate INSIDE each union arm before the limit and says why (packages/db/migrations/0202_list_activity_p_work.sql:54-61 and :394-403, 'a p_work test applied to the unioned page would reproduce server-side the exact defect'; :435-440 skips the ar arm entirely). With a 16-row fixture nothing is observable today and the absent-p_work shape is byte-identical (verified: the new '#853 - every existing shape' cell, plus activity-feed-walk 17/17 re-run here), but the ticket's own named successor - a Work Activity walk - would be asserting against a mock that pages differently from the door. The next_cursor/truncated change is also behaviour the brief did not ask for.
findings.required_fix: Filter the fixture BEFORE the page/limit is taken (or state in the handler's comment that the mock models one page only, and why), and keep cursor/truncated semantics a filtered page would really carry.

findings.title: 'No behavioural change to any lane's responses' is stronger than what was proven
findings.evidence: The report's #862 section says 'every repoint is a pure plumbing swap'. It is not purely mechanical in principle: the four uncached readers (accrual, counterparty-identity, knowledge, operator-support) returned {} whenever a sibling had already drained the stream through readCachedJson (apps/web/e2e/serve-built.mjs:397 aliases readCachedJson as readJson and reads bodies itself at :453-545, :657, :1018, :1093), so a handler that previously fell through on an empty body can now match and answer. That IS the fix, but it is a behavioural change in those lanes' dispatch, not a no-op. The evidence for 'no harm' is the walks, and those are green (re-run here: accrual-walk 14/14, home-board-walk 27/27, plus the lane's own seven others).
findings.required_fix: Re-word as 'the only behavioural change is that these handlers now see the real body where they could previously see {}; every lane walk stays green', rather than 'no behavioural change'.
